findings.summary: The ordered-startup counterfactual can leak its gated owner and worker tasks when an assertion fails before release.
findings.diagnosis: exercise_ordered_startup performs the lifecycle_started ordering assertion before release.set(), while complete_before_deadlock_guard recovers blocked tasks only for TimeoutError. If the behavior under test regresses by starting the lifecycle early, line 206 raises immediately, wait_for propagates that AssertionError instead of entering the timeout recovery, and the owner remains blocked on the release event with the facade workers still occupied.
findings.evidence: tests/unit/runtime/test_b102_public_facade_starvation.py:203-209 places both assertions before release.set(); lines 157-167 catch only TimeoutError. The existing failure path in tests/unit/runtime/test_b102_runtime_coordination.py:175-182 explicitly releases the gate and gathers all tasks before reraising an assertion.
findings.correction: Make task cleanup unconditional for every exceptional exit: release the gate and gather or cancel owner/call tasks in a finally/BaseException path, while preserving the special timeout assertion message. Otherwise the exact ordering regression this test is meant to expose can hang executor or event-loop teardown instead of producing a bounded deterministic failure.
